title: Hazel's Grove - The Letter (opening, voice-over sample)

cues.beat: Late spring. The road runs out a little before the Grove does. The last of it is grass, and then a gate.
The gate is stuck. It always was. You lift and push, the way she taught you.
The Grove is overgrown and quiet. On the signpost, under a stone, a letter in your grandmother's hand.
The cottage. The kettle, cold. One cup, washed and turned upside down. For whoever came next.
You sit down on the step, where she used to sit, and open the letter.

cues.text: If you're reading this, I've gone up the hill and I'm not coming down for a while. | Don't be dramatic about it.

cues.beat: It is so exactly her that, for a while, you can't read the next bit.

cues.text: There are two eggs in the long grass. They were waiting for someone with warm hands. | That's *you*.
Rules. One: feed them before you feed yourself. Two: never, ever throw one. Three: when you don't know what to do, sit down next to them, and wait.
Moss will be watching from the hill. He's older than the trees, and twice as stubborn. He'll come down when he decides *you're* worth it.
Love, Gran. | P.S. The gate sticks. Lift and push.

cues.beat: You laugh. It comes out the wrong shape. Something small and grey watches from the top of the western hill.

cues.text: Hello? Oh! You're Hazel's. You've got her chin. I'm Fern, from next door. I've been keeping the trees alive, badly.

cues.beat: She sees the letter in your hand, and her face changes.

cues.text: Is she...?
No. | Not *up* there. Not the way people mean.
I go and look at the flowers. Every week. There isn't a new one. I'd know. I *know* all of them.
She went off at the end of the winter. Big coat, bag of fruit, the walking stick she pretends she doesn't need. Said she had some feeding to do.
She told me you'd come. Didn't say when. I put the stone on the letter so it wouldn't blow away. That was my job.
I'm very proud of the stone, actually.
It's a very good stone.
Thank you. Nobody ever mentions the stone. It's from the stream. I tried four. This one had the right sort of face.

cues.beat: From the long grass, out by the fourth lantern post, something hums. Low, like a kettle thinking about it.
It is warm. Small and damp, and warmer than anything has a right to be. It leans into your hand. Then it leans into it entirely.

cues.text: HEY. New Keeper. Don't move. There's a lantern post behind you and I've nearly fixed it.

cues.beat: A crackle, a small blue flash, and the smell of burnt hair.

cues.text: Fixed it. Mostly. The hair grows back, before you ask. I'm Sparks. I run the fast ones. Yours is cute. Is it fast? It looks fast.
It is three minutes old, Sparks.
Potential, Fern. I'm talking about potential.

cues.beat: Your Nubbin sneezes. A tiny blue spark jumps off the end of its nose.

cues.text: Did you SEE that? It likes *me*. It's caught it off *me*.
That *isn't* how anything works.
Right. Dusk. Watch this.

cues.beat: One by one, the lanterns come up: the pond, the stream, the old wall. Gold on the water.
The fourth, out by the long grass, catches, gutters, and settles into a thin, uncertain flicker.

cues.text: Ugh. That one. New wick, new glass, new everything. Three times.
Has it *ever* worked?
Never has. Not properly. Not since before my time.
Hazel said to leave it be. She'd stand out there some evenings, with it going like that. Just stand.
Like she was waiting for someone to knock.

cues.beat: Nobody says anything for a moment. On the hill, the grey shape has moved one step down.
Morning. Mist on the pond. A woman comes up the lane smelling of salt and weed, with a bucket that slops at every step.

cues.text: Morning. Marina. I keep the tide pools past the ridge. Hazel used to trade me fruit for swimming lessons. For the Nubbins, not for her.
She'll be back. She owes me a bag of plums. Hazel doesn't leave debts.
Oh, and if a man in a grey coat comes by talking about investment, don't sell him anything. Not fruit. Not eggs. Nothing.
Corvin. Runs the Circuit, up the valley. His lot win everything. They're so fast. They're so quiet.
I don't like quiet ones. I like the ones that yell.

cues.beat: Marina looks up the valley the way you would look at weather coming.
Late afternoon. A man in a grey coat stands at the gate. He doesn't lift. He doesn't push. The gate swings open for him, without a sound.

cues.text: Hazel's heir. You have her stubborn little chin. Corvin Vale. I run the Circuit, up the valley. The real races.

cues.beat: He offers his hand. It is cold. Not cool: cold, like a stone lifted out of a winter stream.

cues.text: I knew your grandmother well. I was her student, once. We disagreed about methods. She thought *love* was a method.
Is there one for *her*? | Up there.
No.
No. | There wouldn't be. She'd want to argue with it first.

cues.beat: His hand goes to his coat, to the breast pocket, and rests there.

cues.text: Your young one there. Good bones. I will give you two hundred Shells for it, right now, and it will eat better with me than it ever will here.

cues.beat: Your Nubbin has gone very still behind your legs.

cues.text: No. They're not for sale.
Of course. | Her chin. | The offer stands. Everyone sells eventually, when things get hard. Things always get hard.

cues.beat: He goes. The gate swings shut behind him, on its own. On the top rail, where his hand rested, a thin grey bloom of frost.
Behind your legs, something small lets out a long breath.
